a.text: The girl closes her eyes and lets go as she is told.

The force gripping onto her leg quickly disappears. She can hear all sorts of tiny trinkets splashing into the water. Just before she herself touches the surface of the sea, a force pulls her upward and sends her back to dry land again.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: *cough* *cough* *cough*.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's not easy to control the strength and angle while I'm dealing with a person.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I-It's okay. I'm fine.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Smells herself)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: My bleeding's stopped.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Why are they still so excited? Have there always been so many Sea Terrors here?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Are these the same monsters from last night?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: More or less.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I've never seen them before.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You should stay away from this place for a couple of days. Now go back.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Stop tugging my skirt... You aren't a child.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I just want to say... I think I know what it is that I want now. I want to hear you sing.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: And that's because... I don't know what songs are like. I heard you humming in your sleep, but I didn't understand it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, will you do it? Is this what it means to make a promise?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: More or less.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Frowns)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: My harp.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Huh? Oh yeah, singer, where did your harp go?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'll go look for it...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Okay. I'll help.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: So does this mean you'll come back with me? G-Great!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Is this something to be so happy about?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Hey, Drywall, good morning!

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Sheetmetal...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Oh yeah, where did Sheetmetal go? You never go anywhere without each other.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Sheetmetal.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Are you looking out... to the sea?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Does this mean... It was Sheetmetal who got the red seashell last night?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Woodframe, my condition got worse.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: My chest is bloating like it's about to blow.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: I don't even want to eat. Leave me alone.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, welcome to our home sweet home again!

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Ugh... agh...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Your grandmother...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Grandma Petra is still sleeping. She's been lying down ever since we got back last night.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She's probably tired, getting so worked up like that. I didn't expect her to run out and talk to the Inquisitor like that. She was different.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You're right. That was very amazing. She fought off the Inquisitor.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Hmn... ha...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She fought off.. the Inquisitor?! Singer, if the Inquisitor catches you saying that, she'll be really mad.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't care if she does.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: But if she wants another go...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She won't come to you looking for trouble again, right?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It doesn't matter to me whose trouble she's looking for.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Strokes case)

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Oh, yeah, why don't we go look for your harp?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hold on.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You got stuff on your head.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Whoa! All this green, slimy stuff... W-What is this?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: That's seaweed.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Did it get on my head when I tripped?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Probably.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Is this stuff... useful in any way? Looks kinda like seagrass. Can I use it as bedding once it's dried? Grandma Petra's back is hurting her, so this will come in handy.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Give it to me.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Take some seashells and use them to grind up these seaweeds. Don't wash off the slime.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Add enough seawater to completely cover the seaweeds. Put it all in a jar and seal it up, then wait half a year.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You can drink it once the liquid's greenish color has faded. That's when it's fermented.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer...?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What's wrong? Is there something you didn't understand?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: No... I just don't think you've ever talked to me this much in one go.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Don't throw away your seashells either. Wash them and lay them out to dry. You can use them to drink alcohol and such.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Alcohol? What's that?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's written right there. This place used to be a bar, a place for alcohol.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: So this word means alcohol!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Alcohol can supposedly bring happiness and help us forget all our worries.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Does it work?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Not at all...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It does taste pretty good, though.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Did you drink this stuff often back home...? Back in Ægir?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Not exactly.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I would drink something similar before dances.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It must have been very fun. Oh, I get it now! Alcohol doesn't bring happiness, but we drink alcohol when we're happy!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Does everyone outside, uh, drink alcohol? Is everyone out there always so happy?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Not necessarily.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I get it. They definitely aren't as happy as I am now. Singer, thanks for teaching me how to make alcohol. I really wanna drink it with you right now.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Your hand movement is wrong.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: If you grind it like that, it's not going to grind up very well. Try a different angle. Use the sharpest point and follow the seaweed's pattern.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Control your rhythm and your breathing... Make your hand and your whole body one with the sea breeze that's brushing against your skin.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Like that—One stroke, and it's shredded.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You are staring at me. Do you still want another go? Now that there's only one of you, it'll be over very quickly.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: No... I don't think I will.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: This is yours.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: This is my harp.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Sheetmetal found it.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: He saw you drop it outside last night.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Oh, that's great! Singer, now we don't need to go look for your harp!

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: He brought it back to our house... and... and he told me to give it to you.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: That's all he said before he left...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Huh? Oh...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Plucks strings)

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Huh...? This melody... You were humming it while you were asleep last night.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's always in my head.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Is this a song that you and your partner used to sing?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: We have a lot of songs like this back home. We sing... as a way to talk to each other.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: When I left, the singing was gone too. I'm all by myself, and this song is all that I have left.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: No wonder this song sounds so sad.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Plucks strings)

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, remember our promise?! You got your harp back. Does that mean you can sing for us now?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: We're all waiting. Right, Grandma Petra?

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Mmn... Uhh...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Grandma probably can't talk today. She would sing along with you if she could.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Ah... Ahhh...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, Grandma wants to hear your song.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Alright.

a.text: Clad in her red dress, the wandering singer sits in the middle of the group. She closes her eyes as her fingers stroke the strings of her harp.

The notes and the lyrics flow out from her naturally as she plunks away at her harp strings, permeating every corner of the rundown bar. The melody twists and expands in the air as though this is where it belongs.

steps.text: A hunter is walking on seacoast way♪
With homeland left a mile behind, his path lies ahead♪
From his forebears and children, he was torn♪
Into the seas his lover was swept away, floating in the deep, dead♪

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: I noticed a change in your expression. Did you feel something, perhaps?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Nothing.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Not a surprise. Your reflexes are still rather slow. Look at the water before you. The fluctuation of the level, the frequency of the waves, and the movement of its luster. All of these are information.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: It'll be high tide soon. We should go.
A hunter is walking on seacoast way♪
With homeland left a mile behind, they must lament and pray♪
There is no end to his path♪
The road ahead is shrouded in gray♪

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: She's singing.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: How could she sing in front of these people in this rundown house?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: And... they are listening to her.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: The ones who hang their heads are still looking straight at the floor. The ones who don't speak are still silent as ever. Her singing has no way to reach their cold, hard husks, but their eyes...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Do they understand it somehow?

a.text: A hunter is walking on seacoast way♪
The singer stops her fingers, but the harmony formed by her harp and voice together does not simply disappear because of that.
It yet remains with the wanderer herself, creating an open seam in the thick dust.
A few sprouts land in that crevice just as others begin to sprout from it.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Grandma Petra?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She... fell asleep.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She never sleeps so peacefully. Most of the time, she starts screaming the moment she closes her eyes, grasping at nothing.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I thought she'd want to dance when she heard you sing. I mean, she's always chirping about how she wants to dance.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Drywall?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: I'm going to die. There's seawater in my eyes... It's salty. Not tasty at all.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Whoa... Are you... crying?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Crying? What is that?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's a kind of emotion that flows out from the deepest depths of your body...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: It is...? I don't think I understand.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, I like your songs. You don't like to talk, but you have so much to tell when you are singing.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Could you sing it again? I want to hear you talk about lots more.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Plucks strings)

a.text: The sea breeze envelops the singer's fingers and wafts into her nostrils. The smell here has changed.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant C
steps.text: Food...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant D
steps.text: We'll have food again...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant C
steps.text: To the beach.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant D
steps.text: Priest!

a.text: The melody of her song has stopped.
